texts.facts: Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10661700/ 1 1. The Detailed Accident Report (DAR) was filed on 22.03.2023 and was registered as a Motor Accident Claim petition. The DAR revealed that a Road Traffic Accident took place on 10.11.2022 at about 03:30 am at Hanuman Mandir, Yamuna Bazar, Kashmere Gate, Delhi wherein Sh. Ajay Bhati had sustained grievous injury. The accident took place with the vehicle bearing registration No. DL1GC4981 driven rashly and negligently by respondent no. 1 Mangla Prasad, owned by respondent no.2, Santosh Kumar Tripathi and insured with respondent no.3, the New India Assurance Company. BRIEF FACTS 2. The brief facts that have emerged from the DAR are that on 10.11.2022, on receipt of information of an accident vide DD No. 13A, the information of present accident was handed over to IO/ASI Admane Madhukar. He went to the spot where friend of injured met and informed that the injured was taken to Trauma Center. HC Rajesh also came to the spot and after leaving him at the spot, IO went to the Trauma Center and he found injured vide MLC No. 2644/2023 namely Ajay Bhati. IO collected the MLC from the hospital and recorded the statement of the injured. Thereafter, IO registered FIR on basis of statement of injured and MLC under Section 279/337 IPC. 3. During the course of investigation, IO went to the spot and prepared the site plan. IO found both the vehicles involved in the accident at the spot, which he took into his custody. No CCTV footage RUCHIKA by RUCHIKA SINGLA SINGLA Date: 2026.02.05 12:58:43 +0530 found from the spot. Thereafter, owner of the offending vehicle was served with notice U/s 133 MV Act to which he replied that at the time of accident, the vehicle was driven by Sh. Mangla Prasad and the driver was handed over to the IO. IO interrogated him and arrested him and documents of the offending vehicle and the offending vehicle were taken by the IO in his custody. Further, Sh. Mangla Prasad produced his surety and he was released on bail. Thereafter, IO verified the documents of the offending vehicle from the concerned authority which were found to be correct. Both the vehicles were got mechanically examined by the IO and the vehicles were released on superdari. 4. Thereafter, MLC was deposited in the hospital for final opinion and the injuries were opined to be "grievous". Upon this IO changed Section 337 to Section 338 IPC. After completion of investigation, chargesheet for the offences u/s 279/338 IPC was filed against the driver of the offending vehicle, Mr Mangla Prasad before the concerned Ld. JMFC and the DAR was filed before this Tribunal. WRITTEN STATEMENTS 5. WS was filed by the respondent no.1 and 2 on 26.05.2023. It was stated by the respondents that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the petitioner as he was driving his motorcycle at a fast speed carrying two pillion riders, in violation of the traffic rules. Further, it is stated that the petitioner had hit the vehicle of the respondents from behind. It was stated that the respondent no.1 was driving his vehicle as per the traffic rules and regulations and there was no negligent driving on his behalf. Hence, it is stated that the accident Digitally signed RUCHIKA by RUCHIKA SINGLA SINGLA Date: 2026.02.05 12:58:52 +0530 was not caused by the respondents Ajay Bhati(D)I(581/22/Kg) vs Mangla Prasad(New India) on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10661700/ 2 and they were not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner. 6. Separate WS was filed on behalf of respondent no. 3. It was admitted that the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent no. 2 company vide policy No. 36170031220100000460 valid from 01.06.2022 to 31.05.2023. However, it was stated that no liability could be imposed on the respondent no.3 unless the rash and negligent act of the respondent no.1 could be proved. OPP 2. If so, to what amount and from whom? OPP. 3. Relief. PETITIONER 'S EVIDENCE 8. The petitioner/injured examined himself as PW-1. He tendered his evidence by way of affidavit which is Ex.PW-1/A and the same bears his signatures at points-A & . He relied upon the following RUCHIKA RUCHIKA SINGLA SINGLA Date: 2026.02.05 12:58:58 +0530 documents: 1. Copy of Aadhar Card is Ex. PW1/1. 2. The MLC of deponent is Ex. PW1/2. 3. The chargesheet/DAR alongwith documents is Ex. PW1/3 (colly). 4. Original medical record/bills are Ex. PW1/4 (colly). 9. Thereafter, PW1 was duly cross examined by the Ld. Counsel for respondents. Thereafter, PE was closed vide order dated 10.11.2025. It was stated by the Ld. Counsels for respondents that no evidence was to be led on behalf of respondents. Hence, RE was closed vide order dt. 23.12.2025. FINAL ARGUMENTS 11. The Petitioner has filed his duly filled Form XIV and financial statement of the injured was recorded. The onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioner. It is the case of the petitioner that on 10.11.2022 at about 03:50 am, he was returning home from Daryaganj on his motorcycle and reached at Hanuman Mandir, Yamuna Bazar, Kashmere Gate, Delhi, when the driver of the offending vehicle i.e. the respondent no. 1 came very fast and carelessly in a negligent manner and hit his vehicle with great force. It is stated that due to the said accident, the petitioner fell from his vehicle and he suffered injuries. The petitioner has reiterated the said facts on oath as PW1. The petitioner/injured has claimed Rs. 40,000/- for loss due to mental shock. Loss of amenities: 47. The petitioner/injured has claimed Rs. 30,000/- under this head. Loss of marriage prospects 48. The petitioner/injured has not claimed any amount under this head. Disfiguration: 49. The petitioner/injured has claimed Rs. 20,000/- under this head. RUCHIKA by SINGLA SINGLA Date: 2026.02.05 13:01:08 +0530 Loss of earning, inconvenience, disappointment, frustration, mental stress, dejectment and unhappiness in future life etc.: 50. The petitioner has claimed a sum of Rs. 40,000/- under this head. Considering the nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner, a sum of Rs. 30,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under this head. Future medical expenses: 51. He has placed on record an OPD receipt dated 28.04.2025 issued by Dr. Deepak Kumar Arora, Max Hospital as per which he has been advised Corrective Osteotomy with Plate. Osteotomy involves a procedure to correct alignment (e.g., bow legs/knock knees), shorten or lengthen bones, and relieve pressure on damaged joint cartilage. RUCHIKA SINGLA SINGLA Date: 2026.02.05 13:01:17 +0530 54. The estimate for the said procedure issued by Max Hospital is also placed on record as per which the charges for an economy bed shall be Rs. 2,62,450/-. In MACT cases, the compensation is awarded under various heads and if by treatment, the injured can improve his living condition as Ajay Bhati(D)I(581/22/Kg) vs Mangla Prasad(New India) on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10661700/ 13 were prior to the accident, then such cost can be awarded to the injured. In view of the same, the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs. 2,62,450/- towards future medical expenses. 55. Further, a lumpsum amount of Rs. 2,00,000/- is awarded for post surgery care, attendant, special diet, follow up etc. Hence, a total sum of Rs. 4,62,450/- is awarded to the petitioner for future medical expenses and care. In the case of Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Niru @ Niharika & Ors. SLP no. 22136 of 2024 decided on 14.07.2025, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has upheld awarding of 9% interest per annum. Therefore, it is held that the petitioner shall be entitled to interest @ 9% per annum from the date of filing of DAR i.e. 22.03.2023 till realization. However, vide order dated 19.08.2025, it was directed that the petitioner would not be entitled to interest from that day till conclusion of PE. The PE was concluded on 10.11.2025. Hence, the petitioner would not be entitled to interest from 19.08.2025 to Digitally signed by RUCHIKA RUCHIKA SINGLA SINGLA Date: 2026.02.05 13:01:31 +0530 10.11.2025. DISBURSEMENT 58. The Financial Statement of petitioner/injured was recorded by this Court/Tribunal. As per the said statement, the monthly expenses of his family are approximately Rs. 50,000/- per month.
texts.arguments: It is further submitted that both the vehicles were found at the spot by the IO. The petitioner was treated at the hospital wherein it has specifically mentioned that the injuries are due to a road traffic accident. Hence, it is submitted that it is proved that the respondent no. 1 was driving the negligent in a rash and negligent manner due to which the petitioner suffered injuries. 14. Per contra, it is submitted by Ld. Counsel for respondent no. 3 that the petitioner was inebriated at the time of the accident. Further, he had 4 other persons on his motorcycle and thus, he lost balance of the same. Hence, the petitioner is completely liable for the said accident. Digitally signed by RUCHIKA RUCHIKA SINGLA SINGLA In Bimla Devi & Ors. v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors (2009) 13 SC 530, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India that negligence must be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view must be adopted in reaching a conclusion. In National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 and United India Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Deepak Goel & Ors, 2014 (2) TAC 846 (Del) decided by the Coordinate Bench of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court, it was held as under :- "......where the claimants filed either the certified copies of the criminal record or the criminal record showing the completion of investigation by police or issuance of charge sheet under Section 279/304A IPC or the certified copy of FIR or the recovery of the mechanical inspection report of RUCHIKA SINGLA by RUCHIKA SINGLA Date: 2026.02.05 12:59:20 +0530 the offending vehicle, then these documents are sufficient proof to reach to a conclusion that the driver was negligent particularly when there is no defence available from the side of driver." 18. Reliance is also being placed upon the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Meera Devi, 2021 LawSuit (Del) wherein it was held that "......in view of Delhi Motor Accident Claim Tribunal Rules, 2008, contents of DAR has to be presumed to be correct and read in evidence without formal proof of the same unless proof to the contrary was produced." Both the involved vehicles were found by the IO at the spot in an accidental condition. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. In Mohammed Siddique vs National Insurance Company (2020) 2 SCALE 565, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that: "12. It is seen from the material on record that the accident occurred at about 2:00 a.m. on 5.09.2008. The relevant portion of paragraph 4 of the order of the High Court reads as follows: "On careful assessment of the evidence led, this Court finds substance in the plea of the insurance company. 28. Secondly, it is argued by Ld. Counsel for respondent no.3 that the petitioner was under the influence of liquor at the time of the accident. In the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors. , Hon'ble Supreme Court held as under: "General principles relating to compensation in injury cases 4. The provision of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (`Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. 9 5 . The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following : Pecuniary damages (Special Damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. 35. Per contra, Ld. Counsel for respondent no. 3 has argued that no evidence has been led by the petitioner to prove the said income. However, as no evidence for the same has been led, his income may be assessed as per the minimum wages. The petitioner is claiming a sum of Rs. 15,000/- towards special diet. Although, there is no bill to support his plea, but keeping in view the nature of injury suffered by the petitioner, it seems that he must have required special diet and must have incurred expenditure towards special diet, therefore, a sum of Rs. 15,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under the head of special diet. Conveyance charges: 43. The petitioner is claiming a sum of Rs. 15,000/- towards conveyance charges. Admittedly there is no document showing expense on conveyance, however, considering his injuries and repeated visits to the hospital, this Tribunal is of the view that the petitioner must have spent money on conveyance thus, the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs. 15,000/- towards conveyance charges. Attendant charges: 44. The petitioner has claimed a sum of Rs. 15,000/- towards attendant charges. Admittedly there is no document showing expense on an attendant. However, considering the period of treatment of the petitioner and his injuries, the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs. 15,000/- towards attendant charges. Pain & Suffering: 45. The petitioner/injured has claim Rs. 50,000/- under the head pain and suffering. It is submitted by Ld. Counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner has to undergo a Corrective Osteotomy procedure as advised by the concerned doctor. The estimate cost of the procedure is proved as Ex. PW1/4. 59. The Hon'ble Delhi High Court vide orders dated 07.12.2018 & 08.01.2021 in FAO No. 842/2003 under the title Rajesh Tyagi & Ors. Vs. Jaivir Singh & Ors. has given the following directions: "(i) The bank shall not permit any joint name to be added in the saving account or fixed deposit accounts of the claimants i.e. saving bank accounts of the claimants shall be an individual saving bank account and not a joint account. (vi) The bank shall make an endorsement on the passbook of the claimant to the effect, that no cheque books and/or debit card have been issued and shall not be issued without the permission of the Court and the claimant shall produced the passbook with the necessary endorsement before the Court for compliance." 60. However, in a recent judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India titled as Parminder Singh vs Honey Goyal on 18 March, 2025 in S.L.P. (C) No. 4484 OF 2020 has held that : "17.
